# Expressions in testdata/adversarial that the JDK's XPath answers and this package
# deliberately does NOT: they use constructs outside the transform subset documented in
# doc.go and transform.go, which is driven by what the upstream dss-xades corpus actually
# contains.
#
# This file is a statement about the Go side, not an oracle answer - unlike every other
# file under testdata/, it is written by hand. Its job is to keep the gap honest in both
# directions. TestTransformAdversarialKnownAnswers requires that
#
#   * every expression listed here is refused by CompileTransform with an *UnsupportedError,
#     never approximated and never answered; and
#   * every expression NOT listed here compiles and matches the JDK node for node.
#
# So widening the subset fails the test until the line is deleted, and narrowing it fails
# the test until a line is added - neither can happen quietly. A ds:XPath transform using
# one of these constructs is a signature this port cannot validate and Santuario can; that
# is an availability gap, and it is a refusal rather than a wrong answer, which is the side
# to fail on.
#
# One expression per line, verbatim.

count(ancestor-or-self::*) < 10
count(ancestor-or-self::ds:Signature) = 1
count(namespace::*) > 2
count(preceding-sibling::*) > 1
ancestor-or-self::n7 and not(ancestor-or-self::ds:Signature)
number(.) > 0 or number(.) = 0
position() = last()
string-length(normalize-space(.)) > 4
